coordinates.note: Coordinate is the original SNO detector's own published position (converted from 46 deg 28' 30'' N, 81 deg 12' 04'' W); SNOLAB is the expansion of that same cavern/site, so this is used as the SNOLAB underground-lab marker. This supersedes the earlier OpenStreetMap-only campus-level point (which is kept as an additional, lower-rank source for the surface/general area).
coordinates.quote: The SNO detector is located at 46 28' 30'' N, 81 12' 04'' W in the INCO, Ltd., Creighton mine near Sudbury, Ontario, Canada.

depth.note: The SNO paper gives 2039 m to the detector-vessel centre; the SNOLAB facility page separately states a 2070 m rock overburden at the 6800 ft level. Both are kept: this field records the more precise, sourced vessel-depth figure.
depth.quote: The center of the detector vessel is 2039 m below the surface in a cavity excavated from the "6800-foot" level of the mine.

depth_mwe.note: The SNO collaboration's 2009 muon-flux paper gives 5890 ± 94 m.w.e. for a flat overburden at 2.092 km, and Mei & Hime 2006 Table I use 6.011 ± 0.1 km.w.e.; the three figures agree within about 2%.
depth_mwe.quote: The granitic rock overburden (mainly norite) corresponds to approximately 6000 m water equivalent.

muon_flux.locator: Abstract and Sec. V.A (Cosmic-Ray Muon Flux), Phys. Rev. D 80, 012001 (arXiv:0902.2776)
muon_flux.note: Total flux of cosmic-ray muons measured with the SNO detector in its cavern, for zenith angle cos θ > 0.4 (the flat overburden removes almost all muons at larger angles) and corrected for acceptance: 62.9 ± 0.2 muons per day through a circular fiducial area of 830 cm radius. The paper places the detector at a depth of 2.092 km, 5890 ± 94 m.w.e. with a flat overburden. Independent check in the SNOLAB Cube Hall: DEAP-3600 (arXiv:2608.20504, 20 Aug 2026) finds (3.71 ± 0.25 stat. ± 0.09 syst.) × 10^-10 cm^-2 s^-1 by coincidence, 1.4 sigma from SNO, and 4.42 ± 0.13 ± 0.84 from its water tank alone. Second source: Mei & Hime 2006, Table I, Sudbury row, (3.77 ± 0.41) × 10^-10 cm^-2 s^-1 at 6.011 ± 0.1 km.w.e. from an earlier SNO report. Vertical intensity not recorded. The quote writes the unit as muons/s/cm2, the same as cm^-2 s^-1; its factor 10^-10 multiplies the whole bracket, so the stored value is 3.31 × 10^-10 cm^-2 s^-1.
muon_flux.quote: The cosmic ray muon flux at SNO with zenith angle cos θzenith > 0.4 is measured to be (3.31±0.01 (stat.)±0.09 (sys.))×10−10 µ/s/cm2

name: SNOLAB underground laboratory
notes: The water-equivalent depth and the underground-laboratory coordinate are sourced to the original SNO detector paper (Nucl. Instrum. Meth. A449 (2000) 172), not to Wikipedia.

summary.plain: The underground part of SNOLAB, reached through an active nickel mine two kilometres below the surface near Sudbury, Canada.
summary.technical: Underground laboratory complex at the 6800 ft level of Vale's Creighton mine (~2070 m norite rock overburden), 1.8 km from the 9 Shaft entrance; an expansion of the original SNO cavern into a Class-2000 clean-room facility.
